newsitem.title: OMAN: Israel trade office sees no threat to Oman links.
newsitem.headline: Israel trade office sees no threat to Oman links.

text.p: Israel sees no threat to its commercial links with Gulf Arab Oman over Middle East policies of the new hardline government of the Jewish state, the head of the Israeli trade mission said on Tuesday.
"There is no threat to the relationship between Israel and Oman. Oman really supports the peace process," Oded Ben-Haim told Reuters in an interview.
"I do see the future not (only) in trade but in joint ventures. Business is willing to invest in the countries, willing to transfer know-how and have trust," he said.
But first "we have to build our reputation from scratch".
Oman and Qatar have forged ahead of other Gulf states in establishing economic ties with Israel but have stopped short of full diplomatic relations.
The Israel Trade Representation Office opened in Muscat in May and last month Oman's commercial office opened in Tel Aviv.

Israel's hardline Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu angered Arab states by challenging the key principle of land-for-peace and not carrying out some measures agreed under peace accord between the Palestinians and the previous Israeli government.

Oman and Qatar in August urged Israel to resume negotiations with Arabs on the agreed principles of the peace process which had paved the way for the swapping of the trade missions between the two states and the Jewish state.

Oman's trade representative in Israel has said Netanyahu's election did not prompt second thoughts about opening the office. But Qatar delayed opening its trade office in Tel Aviv in reaction to Netanyahu's policies.

"We did not cut our ties with Tel Aviv and their office is open in Doha but we delayed the opening of our office for a certain period and contacts are less than before," Qatar Foreign Affairs Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani said in a recent interview with Kuwait's al-Rai al-Aam newspaper.
Ben-Haim said the first step towards stronger economic ties with Oman was cooperation in farming and water management.

"The first thing I want to see is cooperation in agriculture, which is the cornerstone of building cooperation with Egypt. We train 700 Egyptians every year in agricultural technology and if we can do it here, I will be happy," he said.
